cards: Mahmud of Ghazni was ruler of the Ghaznavid Empire from 998 to 1030, from his capital at Ghazni in Afghanistan.
William the Conqueror was Duke of Normandy from 1035 and King of England from 1066, after defeating Harold II at Hastings.
Alfonso VI of Castile was king of León and Castile in the late eleventh century.
Adam of Bremen was a German chronicler who wrote the Deeds of the Bishops of Hamburg, a history of the archbishopric of Hamburg-Bremen, around 1075.
Harold Godwinson was the last crowned Anglo-Saxon King of England, reigning as Harold II from January to October 1066.
Sancho III, called the Great, was king of Pamplona (Navarre) from about 1004 to 1035 and the most powerful ruler of Christian Spain.
Basil II was Byzantine emperor from 976 to 1025, one of the most successful rulers of the empire.
Yaroslav the Wise was Grand Prince of Kiev from 1019 to 1054, after a long war of succession among the sons of Vladimir the Great.
Alp Arslan was sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1063 to 1072.
Cnut the Great was a Danish prince, son of Sweyn Forkbeard, who conquered England in 1016 and became king of Denmark in 1018 and of Norway in 1028.
Conrad II was the first Salian king of Germany, elected in 1024 and crowned emperor in Rome in 1027.
Malik Shah I was sultan of the Seljuk Empire from 1072 until his death in 1092, when the empire reached its greatest extent.
Olaf Haraldsson, later Saint Olaf, was King of Norway from 1015 to 1028.
Vladimir Monomakh was Prince of Pereyaslavl and Chernigov and, from 1113, Grand Prince of Kiev.
Rajendra Chola I was an emperor of the Chola dynasty of southern India in the early eleventh century.
Tughril, or Tughril Beg, was the founder of the Seljuk Empire.
Robert Guiscard was a Norman adventurer of the Hauteville family who became Duke of Apulia and Calabria in 1059.
El Cid, Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, was a Castilian nobleman and soldier.
Pope Urban II was bishop of Rome from 1088 to 1099.
Alexios I Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1081 to 1118 and founder of the Komnenian dynasty.
Edward the Confessor was king of the English from 1042 to 1066, the son of Æthelred the Unready and Emma of Normandy.
Godfrey of Bouillon was Duke of Lower Lorraine and a leader of the First Crusade, son of Count Eustace II of Boulogne.
Henry, Count of Portugal, was a Burgundian noble who fought for Alfonso VI of León against the Almoravids.
Ramanuja was a Hindu philosopher and theologian, the leading teacher of the Sri Vaishnava tradition of South India.
Airlangga was a Javanese king who founded the kingdom of Kahuripan in East Java.
Anawrahta was king of Pagan from 1044 to 1077 and is regarded as the founder of the first Burmese empire.
Gruffydd ap Llywelyn was king of Gwynedd and Powys from 1039 and, from about 1055, ruler of nearly all of Wales, the only king ever to unite it.
Henry III, of the Salian dynasty, was king of Germany from 1039 and Holy Roman Emperor from 1046.
Matilda of Canossa was margravine of Tuscany and ruler of wide lands in northern Italy, including Modena, Reggio, Mantua and Ferrara.
Rudolf III was the last king of the Kingdom of Burgundy, also called Arles, reigning from 993 to 1032.
Yusuf Balasaguni was a Turkic poet and statesman from Balasagun, in modern Kyrgyzstan, under the Kara-Khanid Khanate.
Boris and Gleb were sons of Vladimir the Great of Kiev who were murdered in 1015 during the succession struggle after their father's death, a crime the chronicles blame on their brother Sviatopolk.
Suleiman ibn Qutalmish was a Seljuk prince who founded the Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia.
Abu Bakr ibn Umar was an Almoravid leader of the Lamtuna Berbers in the eleventh century.
Anna of Kiev was a daughter of Yaroslav the Wise who became queen of France as the wife of Henry I, whom she married in 1051.
Baldwin I of Jerusalem, earlier known as Baldwin of Boulogne, was a leader of the First Crusade.
Bermudo III was king of León from 1028 until 1037, the last of the male line descended from the Astur-Leonese kings.
Bi Sheng was a Chinese artisan of the Song Dynasty credited with inventing movable type printing using ceramic characters around 1040 CE.
Bohemond I of Antioch was a Norman leader of the First Crusade, eldest son of Robert Guiscard.
Ferdinand I, called the Great, was a son of Sancho III of Navarre who received the county of Castile and became king of León in 1037 after killing Bermudo III in battle.
